dedupe_keys.name: multi scanning lidar measurements for resource assessment a case study in complex terrain

description: Santos, Pedro and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The completed ALEX17 campaign uses four scanning instruments in Navarre, on a ridge and mountain range six kilometres apart, with measurements at 125 m above ground. Campaign and flow-result descriptions span 2017–2018 and are grouped as one field evaluation family. The case supports comparison of modelled and observed wind flow in the named terrain. Related campaign reports do not establish identical temporal coverage for every instrument or unrestricted access to every raw measurement. Coverage is limited to the stated models, observations and application settings. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; software and companion-data terms are distinguished where separately established. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected; linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
